1. The browser asks.
  2. The load balancer sends /api/* and /health to the api and everything else to web.
  3. The api writes demo_items and outbox in one transaction: both or neither.
  4. And answers. The visitor's wait ends here.
  5. The api's outbox relay, a thread of its own, sends what outbox holds to the items queue as item.created v1. Two replicas of the api never send the same row twice.
  6. The worker's consumer receives it.
  7. And writes receipts, in the worker's own schema. A second delivery of the same event changes nothing.
  8. It publishes to the results queue as item.processed v1. Only then does it delete the event it received.
  9. The api's results consumer receives it.
  10. And writes item_processing, in the api's own schema.

A service that is down loses nothing: its events wait in the queue. An event that fails 3 times moves to its dead-letter queue, where an alarm waits.
